title: US equity-open opening-range breakout on 15m, anchored to New York time, flat at the US close

source.title: Intraday Trading of Overactive Stocks via Opening Range Breakout (CXO Advisory summary of Zarattini, Barbon and Aziz)

rule_summary: Chart 15m, closed bars only; signal at a bar close, filled at the next bar open. Every time below is New York local time converted to UTC for each date, so 09:30 ET is 13:30 UTC in US daylight time and 14:30 UTC in standard time. Trade only Monday to Friday. OPENING RANGE: the single 15m bar opening at 09:30 ET; ORH = its high, ORL = its low. The day is armed only if 0.003 <= (ORH-ORL)/ORL <= 0.025. ENTRY: the first 15m bar opening between 09:45 and 14:30 ET (inclusive) that closes above ORH, on an armed day, with no open position. Buy at the next open. At most one trade per day, no re-entry after an exit. STOP: ORL, checked intrabar. EXIT: if the stop has not been hit, sell at the open of the 16:00 ET bar, i.e. after the 15:45 ET bar closes. No take-profit. No daily or 1h filters. Holding time is always under 7 hours.
mechanism: Crypto order flow now runs on Wall Street hours. A Kraken study reported by CryptoSlate ('Crypto never closes, but Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP and Solana now move on Wall Street time') finds about half of daily variance falls in 13-22 UTC, with the peak hour shifting with US daylight saving time. So the cash open, not a fixed UTC hour, is when ETF authorised participants, basis traders and US desks start trading. Zarattini et al. read early opening-range direction as one-sided institutional demand that is worked through the session, which runs over range sellers and passive liquidity at the high. The hold is a full US session at peak volatility, so winners should be well above the 0.30-0.45% cost, and losses are capped at ORL (at most 2.5%).
